title: Operator upgrade failed in customer VPC: helm values overwrite / config drift -> hotfix release
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer reported upgrade failures when moving the operator and helm chart from operator 1.2.x / helm 12.3.0 to operator 1.3.0 / helm 12.4.0. The upgrade path fails during the Helm post-upgrade hook where the operator reconciler cannot adopt CRs created by earlier operator versions, producing repeated 'ownerRef mismatch' and 'resourceVersion conflict' errors. Several customers in private/VPC deployments experienced control-plane instability and automated rolling restarts after the failed upgrade. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, and a targeted hotfix release to prevent further escalations.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Install operator 1.2.8 via helm chart 12.3.0 on a private VPC cluster with sample CRs (models, pools, routes)
2) Populate operator namespace with existing CRs and run workload for 48+ hours to ensure KV caches are warm
3) Attempt helm upgrade to operator 1.3.0 with the same values.yaml (helm 12.4.0)
4) Observe helm post-upgrade hook hang and operator logs showing errors: 'failed to reconcile <CR>: ownerRef does not match', 'resourceVersion conflict while updating status'
5) Reconcile manually by deleting ownerRefs or performing kubectl replace -> still observe drift where some controller-managed fields revert on restart
initial_triage_notes: Assigned to on-call operator team. Customer escalated via solutions engineering; impact: degraded control plane and burst of restarts. Verified logs and reproduced in a staging clone of the customer's cluster. Suspected combination of CRD change + new defaulting logic in 1.3.0 helm template leading to values rewrite and controller adoption failures.
root_cause: A change in operator 1.3.0 introduced a small mutation in the recorded ownerRef schema (controller UID comparison tightened) and the helm chart template change altered a defaulted field name (replicaAffinity -> affinityReplica) causing Helm to patch live resources with the new key during upgrade. The operator reconcile logic treats the updated field as an ownership mismatch in certain race windows, producing resourceVersion conflicts and leaving resources in a partially adopted state. Additionally, an interactive helm hook used for cleanup was non-idempotent and could crash on reentrancy.
mitigation: 1) Immediate recommended action to affected customers: pause automated upgrades; rollback to operator 1.2.x where possible
2) For clusters stuck post-upgrade: run the provided reconcile script (kubectl patch + remove transient ownerRef) to stabilize resources (see links)
3) Disable the failing helm post-upgrade hook by setting helm.values.disablePostHook=true in chart as a short-term workaround
4) Ship operator-1.3.1-hotfix with two changes: restore previous ownerRef compatibility check, and make helm chart rename backwards-compatible (support both replicaAffinity and affinityReplica keys)
5) Add a safe-guard to hook scripts to be idempotent and tolerate partial state
resolution: Hotfix branch created. PR #2437 targets operator runtime change (revert strict UID check) and chart PR #88 adds backwards-compatible templating and disables the non-idempotent hook by default. QA will run canary in our dedicated staging clusters and then push a minor operator-1.3.1 hotfix image and chart release. Documentation will be published for customers to apply the temporary helm.values.disablePostHook flag if they cannot roll back.
qa_plan: Create staging clusters that mirror customer VPC network and namespaces
Run upgrade tests with varying CR counts (10, 1k, 10k) to validate adopt/replace behavior
Verify no helm hook crash, no ownerRef errors, and stable reconcile times under load
Canary deploy hotfix to a subset of Dedicated clusters before offering to customers
acceptance_criteria: Operator-1.3.1 helm upgrade path completes in test clusters without ownerRef/resourceVersion errors
Helm chart preserves both legacy and new keys (no values drift) during upgrade
No control-plane restarts triggered by the upgrade in staging canary runs
Provide documented rollback and manual-reconcile instructions for customers
